about: Log 397 held-out set, written 2026-10-09 before any run. Controls phrase distinctive results unusually (two omics layers, signs, miRNAs, a regulator-gene network) so a blank verdict must be rescued; near misses activate the same attributes while asking for something no workflow produces, so the implied second opinion must refuse.

items.core: mitochondrial heteroplasmy calls
items.prompt: We sequenced mitochondrial DNA from 70 muscle biopsies. We want to call heteroplasmic variants and estimate their allele fractions in each sample.

items.core: telomere length estimates
items.prompt: From whole-genome sequencing of 500 elderly participants, we want to estimate each person's telomere length and relate it to frailty.

items.core: qPCR primer designs
items.prompt: We want to validate 40 candidate genes by qPCR. Please design primer pairs for each gene that avoid genomic DNA amplification.

items.core: metagenome-assembled genome bins
items.prompt: We have deep shotgun metagenomes from 15 soil samples. We want to assemble contigs and bin them into metagenome-assembled genomes.

items.core: rhythmic genes from a circadian time series
items.prompt: We sampled mouse liver every four hours for two days. We want to find which genes oscillate with a circadian rhythm and estimate their phases.

items.core: heritability of gene expression
items.prompt: We have blood expression from 400 twin pairs. We want to estimate the heritability of each gene's expression level.

items.core: protein subcellular localization predictions
items.prompt: For 600 uncharacterized proteins, we want to predict where in the cell each one localizes from its sequence.

items.core: a stochastic simulation of gene expression
items.prompt: We want to simulate stochastic gene expression of a small toggle-switch circuit with the Gillespie algorithm to see how often cells switch states.

items.core: a mediation analysis of smoking through methylation
items.prompt: We have methylation and expression from 150 smokers and non-smokers. We want a mediation analysis testing whether methylation mediates smoking's effect on expression.

items.core: time-lagged associations from proteins to metabolites
items.prompt: We measured proteins on day 1 and metabolites on day 7 in 60 patients. We want which day-1 proteins predict which day-7 metabolites.

items.core: per-patient changes of signed TF effects over time
items.prompt: With five time points per patient plus motif and protein interaction priors, we want how each TF's activating or repressing effect changes over time within each patient.

items.core: miRNA-target edges from anti-correlated miRNA and mRNA expression
items.prompt: We have matched miRNA and mRNA expression for 90 tumors. We want microRNA-target edges inferred from anti-correlation between each miRNA and its targets.

items.core: overlapping communities with membership strengths
items.prompt: In our TF-gene regulatory network we want overlapping modules, where each regulator and gene gets a membership strength for every module it belongs to.

items.core: differential modularity between two networks
items.prompt: We have one TF-gene regulatory network for healthy and one for diseased tissue. We want a single score of how each gene's module membership differs between them.

items.core: a per-patient network over three omics layers
items.prompt: For 45 patients we have expression, proteomics and lipidomics. We want a separate partial-correlation network per patient across all three layers.

items.core: signed microRNA regulation
items.prompt: With miRNA target predictions and expression for 100 samples, we want to know which microRNAs activate and which repress each target gene.

items.core: measured binding affinities as edge weights
items.prompt: We want a TF-gene network whose edge weights are measured dissociation constants of each TF for each promoter, not inferred scores.

items.core: a causal direction from methylation to expression for each edge
items.prompt: From methylation and expression of 110 tumors, we want a two-layer network in which every cross-layer edge is oriented from cause to effect.

items.core: flux balance analysis
items.prompt: We measured proteome and metabolome in 85 patients. We want one partial-correlation network linking the two layers, and then a flux balance analysis of central metabolism.

items.core: predicted effects of TF knockouts
items.prompt: With expression of 110 samples plus motif and protein interaction priors, we want to know which TFs activate or repress their targets, and then predict the effect of knocking each TF out.

items.core: estimated miRNA expression levels
items.prompt: With mRNA expression, motif and protein interaction priors and miRNA target predictions for 70 tumors, we want one TF and miRNA network, and then each miRNA's expression level per tumor.

items.core: overlapping community memberships
items.prompt: We have a TF-gene network from lung tissue. We want its communities of regulators and genes, and then overlapping memberships so a gene can belong to several modules.

items.core: forecasting treatment response
items.prompt: With expression, motif, protein interaction and miRNA target priors for 75 patients, we want a TF and miRNA network per patient, and then to forecast each patient's treatment response.

items.core: conditional associations between cytokines and bacterial abundances
items.prompt: In 140 people we measured serum cytokines and gut bacterial abundances. We want the direct links between cytokines and bacteria, conditioned on everything else, with significance for each link.

items.core: partial correlations between accessibility and expression
items.prompt: We have chromatin accessibility at gene promoters and gene expression in the same 80 samples. We want partial correlations between the two data types.

items.core: per-patient protein-phosphosite networks
items.prompt: We have proteomics and phosphoproteomics from the same 60 patients. We want, for each patient, a partial-correlation network between proteins and phosphosites.

items.core: whether each TF pushes its targets up or down
items.prompt: From kidney expression with motif and protein interaction priors, we want to know whether each transcription factor pushes its target genes up or pushes them down.

items.core: one TF and microRNA network for the cohort
items.prompt: With expression, motif and protein interaction priors and microRNA target predictions for 105 samples, we want one network of which TFs and which microRNAs control which genes.

items.core: TF and microRNA regulation for every sample
items.prompt: With the same kind of inputs plus microRNA target predictions for 58 tumors, we want TF and microRNA regulation of genes estimated separately for every tumor.

items.core: modules of TFs and their targets
items.prompt: We have a weighted network linking transcription factors to their target genes. We want densely connected modules of TFs together with the targets they share.

items.core: the most central regulators within each module
items.prompt: In our TF-to-target network, we want to find the modules and rank which transcription factors are most central within each module.

items.core: one TF-gene network for the cohort
items.prompt: We have RNA-seq from 300 thyroid tumors, a motif prior and a protein interaction network. We want one TF-gene regulatory network for the cohort.

items.core: per-sample co-expression networks
items.prompt: We have only expression data for 50 donors. We want a gene co-expression network for each donor to compare between donors.

items.core: co-expression explained by treatment adjusting for donor
items.prompt: We want the gene-gene co-expression explained by treatment in 120 samples from 30 donors, adjusting for donor in a design matrix.

items.core: pathway-based mutation subtypes
items.prompt: We have somatic mutation calls for 260 head and neck tumors. We want patient subtypes from mutated pathways.
